**My reasoning, speaking as myself:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband works in the city now, and my sons too — it is mostly me. I know wheat and corn. My mother grew them, my neighbors grow them. The land here in Quzhou is flat and the soil is good for these two. Every autumn I put in wheat, every summer after harvest I put in corn. That is what makes sense here. I would not try cotton or something new — at my age, I cannot afford a bad gamble.

I buy my wheat seed from the same shop in town as always. It is an improved variety that my neighbor Lanfang has used for three years with good results. For corn, I take whatever hybrid the shop is pushing this season — the owner tells me what is selling well in the village, and it has never done me wrong.

My back is not what it was. I hire the village machine cooperative to do the big rotary plowing before wheat, and they bring the corn planter right after wheat harvest. I do not plow before corn — the machines go straight into the stubble and that saves me money and keeps the soil from drying out too fast.

I irrigate wheat three times: once at planting to get germination, once before the cold sets in around December, and once at heading in April. For corn, summer rain usually handles it but I keep one irrigation ready in case July turns dry. I spray wheat twice — herbicide in winter and something for rust before heading. Corn I spray herbicide once after emergence.

I also keep one mu of land near the house for vegetables — mostly cabbage and garlic — for the family and to sell a little at the village market.
